# Universal Search

5 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 5 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

<!-- END:GENERATED:TOC -->

Universal search fans out one query across many sources in parallel, then fuses, reranks, enriches with top comments, and clusters the results. `/v1/search/everywhere` supports two response modes via the `Accept` header: `application/json` (default, full ranked set) or `text/event-stream` (typed SSE chunks: `meta`, `source_started`, `items`, `source_failed`, `ranked_partial`, `ranked_final`, `comments_enriched`, `clusters`, `done`, `error`). Fully refunded when every source fails or returns empty. Prefer this over fanning out per-platform yourself when the user wants one query across many platforms. `/v1/search/news` is the news sibling: it plans the query into angles with an LLM, localizes each angle per language, and searches Google News editions in up to 12 countries in parallel (50 supported countries), with the same `Accept`-header choice of JSON or SSE and per-leg `query_source` provenance on every article.

## GET /v1/search/creators - 10-24 credits (request-shaped)

Fans a niche query across TikTok user search, Threads user search, and Instagram profile search by default, then merges matching creators into one deterministically ranked list. Ranking is a published formula of query relevance, follower scale, and verification. No LLM rerank by default. Pass `sources=youtube`, `twitter`, or `facebook` (or a CSV of any of the six) to add those profile searches; omitting `sources` keeps the original three-platform walk so existing callers do not change. Pass `brief=` (what you are looking for, in your own words) to have the first 40 creators judged from their name, handle and bio: each gets `brief_match` ({ fits_brief, account_kind, account_kind_confidence, brief_score }) and the list is re-ranked so creators who post about your brief lead, with brands, shops, academies and repost pages below them; `data.brief` reports what was judged and the ranking version. `relevance=filter` also drops creators that do not fit and lists them in `data.brief.dropped_ids`. Pass `country` (CL, AR, MX, CO, PE, EC, UY, ES, BR) to find the creators who post about your query in that market, on TikTok and Instagram, instead of searching account names. The market's own name is added to your query (`inteligencia artificial` with CL searches `inteligencia artificial chile`, returned as `data.country.by_source.<source>.query_sent`). On TikTok the result is the creators behind the videos whose own region is the market and whose text is about your query, with their follower counts. On Instagram it is the profiles a Google search from the market finds, each read from its About this account panel and kept only when the creator declares that country, with followers and bio. Each creator then carries `country` (`{ value, source }`, where source is `post_region` on TikTok and `declared_country` on Instagram) and `evidence` (up to 3 posts or the profile text that found it, with links), and `data.country` counts per source what was kept and what was dropped as another country, off topic or with no country declared. `min_followers`, `verified_only`, `sort` and `brief` work as they do without it. Flat 10 credits with a coverage-based partial refund; with `country`, the searches it runs are billed on top at their own price.

**Use when** you want to find creators about a topic in one call; add country= for one Latin American, Spanish or Brazilian market. search/everywhere covers posts, not profiles.
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · cache 120 s
**Pricing** 10 credits flat, with a coverage-based partial refund. Adding brief= adds 2 credits, refunded when the judging step could not answer for every judged creator. With country=, the searches and lookups it runs are billed on top, each at its own endpoint's price: 1 credit for the TikTok search page, 1 for the Google page and 1 per Instagram profile looked up (at most 10, and free for a profile looked up recently), so at most 12 more. data.legs lists each one with its credits, and the 10 are refunded when no creator is found. A cached page is free.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Niche or topic (2-256 chars), forwarded to every profile search. · e.g. `skincare routine`
- `sources` (optional, string) - Optional CSV allowlist of creator sources (tiktok, threads, instagram, youtube, twitter, facebook). Mutually exclusive with exclude. Omit to keep the default TikTok + Threads + Instagram walk. With country, only tiktok and instagram (the default), and any other source is a free 400. · e.g. `tiktok,instagram`
- `exclude` (optional, string) - Optional CSV blocklist of creator sources. Mutually exclusive with sources.
- `min_followers` (optional, integer, min 0) - Drop fused creators whose follower count is below this integer floor. · e.g. `50000`
- `verified_only` (optional, boolean) - When true, keep only verified creators after fusion. · e.g. `false`
- `sort` (optional, enum: relevance | followers | verification) - Which axis dominates rank: relevance (default), followers, or verification. · e.g. `relevance`
- `brief` (optional, string) - Optional. What you want to find, in your own words (3-300 chars), for example brief=Korean creators who review skincare products. The first 40 creators are judged from their name, handle and bio: does the account post about your brief (fits_brief, 0 to 1), and what kind of account is it (individual_creator, brand_or_business, media_or_publisher, fan_or_repost_page, cannot_tell; null when unsure). With sort=relevance (the default) they are re-ranked so creators who fit and are individual people lead; other sorts keep their order and only gain the labels. These are signals to review, not a finding. Adds 2 credits.
- `relevance` (optional, enum: score | filter) - Optional, only with brief. score (default) ranks and labels; filter also drops judged creators that do not fit the brief and lists them in data.brief.dropped_ids. A creator that could not be judged is never dropped.
- `judgments` (optional, enum: on | off) - Optional. on (default) or off. On, the first 40 creators also carry account ({ account_kind: individual_creator, brand_or_business, media_or_publisher, fan_or_repost_page, cannot_tell or null when unsure, account_kind_confidence, named_person }), judged from their name, handle and bio, and data.account_kinds reports how many were judged. The order is unchanged and it is free. off returns the response without it.
- `country` (optional, enum: CL | AR | MX | CO | PE | EC | UY | ES | BR) - Optional. Two-letter market code (CL, AR, MX, CO, PE, EC, UY, ES, BR) to find the creators who post about your query in that market, instead of searching account names. Runs on TikTok and Instagram: the market's name is added to your query, TikTok creators are kept when the video's own region is the market and its text is about your query, and Instagram creators when they declare that country on their About this account panel. Each creator carries country and evidence, and data.country reports the query sent and what was kept and dropped per source. The searches and lookups it runs are billed on top at their own price, at most 12 credits. Any other code is a free 400.

**Constraints**

- `relevance` is a no-op without `brief` - sending it alone is a free 400.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `creators[].author` {id string, username string, display_name string, bio null, followers number, verified boolean, avatar_url string, url string}; `creators[]` {sources string[], relevance number, follower_rank number, verified boolean, rrf_score number}; `creators[].account` {account_kind string, account_kind_confidence number, named_person number}; `creators_by_source.tiktok[]` {id string, username string, display_name string, bio null, followers number, verified boolean, avatar_url string, url string}; `creators_by_source` {threads array} (+30 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/search/creators" \
  --data-urlencode "query=skincare routine" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/search/everywhere - 20 credits (custom)

Fans out a single query across Reddit, X (ai-search), YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, Threads, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Rumble, Perplexity, and Tavily in parallel by default, with a hashtag endpoint each for TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. A query that contains Hangul also runs `naver`: Naver blog, cafe and KnowledgeiN search in one endpoint, where Korean posts actually are; on other queries it runs only when you pass `sources=naver`. Naver rows carry the corpus in `metadata.corpus`; blog rows have the posting day, KnowledgeiN rows an estimated date (`date_confidence: low`) and cafe rows no date. Facebook public post search runs only when you ask for it: `include=facebook` adds it to the default sources, and `sources=facebook` (alone or beside other sources, for example `sources=facebook,reddit`) runs only the sources you name: it searches newest first inside your date window and returns about 5 posts, each with the post text in `body`, the permalink, the page or person who posted it in `author`, the publish time and like, comment and share counts; the account URL is in `metadata.author_url`. Named beside other sources it has up to 20 seconds, so a request that includes it can take longer. Returns ranked + clustered results, enriched with **real-people comments** on the six endpoints that have a comments surface: Reddit upvoted comments, Hacker News thread replies, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram top-liked comments, and GitHub issue discussion. The other endpoints (X, Threads, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Rumble, Facebook, Polymarket, Perplexity, Tavily) have no comments concept and their rows carry none, so read `top_comments` as absent rather than empty there. The comments per result live at `data.items[i].source_items[0].metadata.top_comments[]`, sorted by score descending, each `{ score, excerpt, truncated, author, url, date }`. Bodies are clipped to 300 characters on a word boundary; a clipped one ends with an ellipsis and sets `truncated: true`, so a short comment is never mistaken for a cut one. GitHub bot accounts are excluded from this block, so a CI deploy-preview or build-status comment never spends the budget. Attribution varies by endpoint, honestly: the Reddit, Hacker News, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and GitHub endpoints are post-shaped and carry an author and a date, while the Perplexity and Tavily endpoints index the open web and have no author to give, so their rows are labelled with the source host. Expect 28 to 30 seconds for a full fan-out; allow a 60s client timeout. On the JSON path the X endpoint (`twitter-ai-search`, an AI-written synthesis of X posts that takes 15 to 45 seconds) runs only when it is the only source requested (`sources=twitter-ai-search`, or `x` / `twitter`); beside other sources it is not run, so it appears in `sources_failed` with a reason saying so and is left out of `sources_called` and `coverage`. Use the streaming path for the X synthesis alongside other sources, or `/v1/twitter/search/tweets` for X posts. Each row's `date_confidence` says how far to trust `published_at`: YouTube rows dated from a "3 years ago" or "2 months ago" label are `low`. Supports streaming via `Accept: text/event-stream` (emits `comments_enriched` chunks per candidate as enrichment lands, before the terminal `done`) and sync via `Accept: application/json`. Flat 20 credits per call regardless of enrichment; a query no source has rows for returns 200 with empty `items` and costs 0 credits.

**Use when** you want a topic's coverage everywhere at once instead of calling each platform's search endpoint yourself. **Not for** a platform you already know, whose own search endpoint is direct, nor for forums only (search/forums), news only (search/news) or creator discovery (search/creators).
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Streaming** Optional SSE - send `Accept: text/event-stream` for incremental frames, or omit it for one JSON body.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search query (1-512 chars) · e.g. `kanye west`
- `lookback_days` (optional, integer, min 1) - Recency window in days (minimum 1, default 30); mutually exclusive with from_date/to_date. This is a ranking signal, not a hard filter: it sets the freshness curve and is forwarded to the sources whose upstream supports date bounds, so a much older item can still rank when nothing recent matches. Windows over 90 days degrade coverage on the sources with no upstream date filtering and emit a warning rather than an error. Check each row's `date_confidence` before filtering on its date: `low` means the date is an estimate (a rounded YouTube label, a KnowledgeiN estimate). · e.g. `30`
- `from_date` (optional, string) - ISO YYYY-MM-DD lower bound; mutually exclusive with lookback_days.
- `to_date` (optional, string) - ISO YYYY-MM-DD upper bound; defaults to today when from_date is set alone.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only rows published at or after this time (ISO 8601 timestamp or date), for polling: pass the previous run's time. A hard filter on `items`, unlike lookback_days; rows with no date are kept and `data.since` reports `{ since, dropped, kept_undated }`. Billed as usual.
- `sources` (optional, string) - Optional CSV allowlist of sources (mutually exclusive with exclude). Valid names: reddit, twitter-ai-search, youtube, tiktok, instagram, hackernews, polymarket, github, threads, pinterest, perplexity, tavily, linkedin, rumble, tiktok-hashtag, instagram-hashtag, youtube-hashtag, naver, facebook. `naver` (Naver blog, cafe and KnowledgeiN) is in the default set only when the query contains Hangul. `facebook` (public post search) runs only when you name it here. Platform shorthands expand to their full group: twitter/x → twitter-ai-search; youtube, instagram, tiktok also include their -hashtag endpoint. Unknown names return a 400. · e.g. `reddit,youtube,github`
- `exclude` (optional, string) - Optional CSV blocklist of sources (mutually exclusive with sources). Same valid names and platform shorthands as sources: excluding youtube/instagram/tiktok also excludes the platform's -hashtag endpoint. Unknown names return a 400.
- `include_transcripts` (optional, boolean) - Fetch spoken-word transcripts for the top 3 video results (default false), so a video whose title never mentions your query but whose narration does can still be found and quoted. Applies to the YouTube, Rumble, TikTok and Instagram endpoints; YouTube and Rumble transcripts carry timestamped segments, TikTok and Instagram are plain text. Transcripts land on `data.items[i].source_items[0].metadata.transcript` and stream as `transcript_enriched` chunks. Included in the flat 20 credits. · e.g. `false`
- `relevance` (optional, enum: filter) - Optional. filter drops the ranked results our relevance judgment already scored as off-topic for your query (unrelated, or clearly about a different thing that shares its words) and lists their ids in data.relevance.dropped_ids, with counts. A result that could not be judged is never dropped; when none could be judged nothing is dropped and data._warnings says relevance_unavailable. items_by_source is not filtered. Omit it to keep every ranked result, ordered as before; each result still carries computed.relevance by default (see judgments). Included in the flat 20 credits.
- `include` (optional, string) - Optional CSV of extra blocks and opt-in sources. facebook adds Facebook public post search to the default sources (it is not in the default fan-out, and `sources=` would replace the defaults instead). stance is now on by default and accepted for compatibility: data.items[i].computed.stance ({ label: positive, negative, neutral, no_opinion or null when unsure, probabilities, confidence }) says what each post, with any replies shown, says about your query, and data.stance_split counts it per platform and overall with the ids behind every count. Posts judged under the confidence floor count as uncertain, never as a stance. If the judgment is unavailable the search still returns, stance is null and data._warnings says stance_unavailable (or stance_skipped when judging was skipped). Included in the flat 20 credits.
- `judgments` (optional, enum: on | off) - Optional. on (default) or off. On, every result also carries data.items[i].computed.stance (see include) and data.items[i].computed.relevance ({ score 0 to 1, on_topic, entity }), with data.relevance counting the off-topic results and listing their ids. Nothing is dropped or reordered and the price does not change. off returns the response without these blocks.
- `switch_from` (optional, string) - Optional brand. data.switch_receipts lists results where the author says they personally left that brand, with the verbatim text, the reason, where they went, and the link. There is no percentage. Rows that are not a switch stay in items. Included in the flat 20 credits.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {candidate_id string, item_id string, source string, title string, url string, snippet string, subquery_labels string[], local_relevance number, freshness number, engagement number, source_quality number, rrf_score number, sources string[]}; `native_ranks` {primary:reddit number}; `source_items[]` {item_id string, source string, title string, body string, url string, author string, published_at string, date_confidence string, relevance_hint number}; `source_items[].engagement` {score number, num_comments number} (+39 more).

Page-level: `data.switch_receipts`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/search/everywhere" \
  --data-urlencode "query=kanye west" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/search/forums - 10 credits (custom)

Fans your topic across Reddit, Hacker News, and Korean forums, RRF-fuses + clusters the threads, and enriches hero threads with their top comments by default (East + West). Naver threads are labeled raw (no comment endpoint). Returns a fused `items[]`, raw per-source buckets, thread clusters, and a deterministic computed block (question_share, top_communities). Each row of `items[].top_comments[]` is `{ score, excerpt, truncated, author, url, date }`. The body is `excerpt`, not `text`: this is the search-endpoint enrichment shape, not the canonical Comment archetype, and it is clipped to 300 characters on a word boundary, with an ellipsis and `truncated: true` when it was cut. `date` is the comment ISO timestamp. Flat 10cr with coverage-based partial refund.

**Use when** you want what real people are asking and answering; search/everywhere also covers video, code, and social posts.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search query (2-256 chars), forwarded to every forum search. · e.g. `airpods pro 3 battery`
- `sources` (optional, string) - Optional CSV allowlist of forum sources (reddit, hackernews, naver_kin, naver_cafe). Mutually exclusive with exclude. · e.g. `reddit,hackernews,naver_kin`
- `exclude` (optional, string) - Optional CSV blocklist of forum sources. Mutually exclusive with sources.
- `comments` (optional, string) - Comment enrichment toggle (on|off, default on). 'off' returns thread-only. · e.g. `on`
- `timeframe` (optional, string) - Recency window passed to Reddit; HN filtered client-side (all|day|week|month|year, default all).
- `lookback_days` (optional, integer) - Alt recency window in days (1-365); HN filtered client-side.
- `relevance` (optional, enum: score | filter) - Optional. Without it every thread already carries items[].computed.relevance ({ p, sense, on_topic }: is the thread about what your query means, or a different thing that shares its words?), free, in the fused order (see judgments). score also reorders threads by relevance blended with their fused rank. filter also drops the threads that are not on topic, lists them in data.relevance.dropped_ids, and counts stance_split, question_share and top_communities over the threads it kept. A thread that could not be judged, or is too short to judge, is never dropped and carries relevance: null. Omit it to keep every thread in the fused order. Included in the flat 10 credits.
- `relevance_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with relevance. The probability (0 to 1) a thread must reach to count as on topic. Default 0.5. Lower keeps more threads, higher keeps fewer.
- `judgments` (optional, enum: on | off) - Optional. on (default) or off. On, every thread also carries items[].computed.relevance ({ p, sense, on_topic }) from the same stance judgment, with data.relevance (mode default) counting it; the fused order is kept and nothing is dropped (relevance=score or filter reorders and drops). off returns the response without it. Included in the flat 10 credits.

**Constraints**

- `relevance_threshold` is a no-op without `relevance` - sending it alone is a free 400.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {title string, url string, source string, container string, enrichable boolean}; `post` {item_id string, source string, title string, body string, url string, author string, published_at string, date_confidence string, relevance_hint number, why_relevant string, snippet string}; `post.engagement` {score number, num_comments number}; `post.metadata` {enrichable boolean}; `post.metadata.top_comments[]` {score number, excerpt string, truncated boolean, author string, url string, date string} (+28 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/search/forums" \
  --data-urlencode "query=airpods pro 3 battery" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/search/multi - 0-30 credits (request-shaped)

Runs the same query on several platforms' native search endpoints at once and returns their rows together: TikTok (`/v1/tiktok/search`), Instagram reels (`/v1/instagram/search/reels`), YouTube (`/v1/youtube/search`), Reddit (`/v1/reddit/search`), Threads (`/v1/threads/search`), X (`/v1/twitter/search/tweets`), Facebook (`/v1/facebook/search/posts`), LinkedIn (`/v1/linkedin/search/posts`) and Telegram (`/v1/telegram/search`, whose rows are channels under `author`, not posts, deduped by handle). `platforms` picks them (default tiktok,instagram,youtube,reddit,threads). Each platform is searched by calling that platform's own endpoint, so every row in `data.items` is exactly the row a direct call returns, with its `post` and `computed` blocks, plus `platform`, and each platform is billed exactly as a direct call would be. Rows are grouped by platform in the order you asked for them, in each platform's own order, and a post URL that already appeared is dropped (`data.duplicates_removed`). Each platform's own filters pass through with a platform prefix, for example `tiktok.region=US` or `reddit.sort=new`. `since` and `until` keep only posts published inside a date window on every platform; a row without a date is kept. Each platform is also sent the native date filter that fits the window, so its one page holds the right posts: Threads and Facebook `start_date` and `end_date`, the X `since:` and `until:` operators, and on TikTok, YouTube and Reddit the narrowest rolling bucket (`date_posted`, `uploadDate`, `timeframe`) that still reaches `since`, for example `tiktok.date_posted=last-3-months` for a date 44 days back. A filter you send yourself is never changed, and `data._warnings` says `window_unreachable` when it cannot reach `since`. On Instagram and LinkedIn the bucket is only suggested, because their date filter changes what the platform returns (Instagram reels lose their view counts). `data.window` reports what each platform was sent (`native`, `origin`, `reaches_since`, `suggested`) and how many of its rows fell outside the window. A newest-first page that ends before `since` (`reddit.sort=new`, X) says `since_not_reached` and names the cursor to continue with. `data.sources` reports each platform: `status` (`ok`, `empty` or `failed`), the rows it returned and kept, the credits it cost, its own `request_id` and `warnings` (for example the note that a Threads query was expanded), and its `next_cursor`, which you send as `cursor` to that platform's own endpoint (listed in `endpoint`) for its next page. This endpoint does not page itself. Native search matches your words literally; `expand=context` also runs up to three short searches written from your query and `relevant_to` (how sellers and posters phrase the same thing), merges them with your query's rows, tags each row with `matched_query`, and reports the searches in `data.expansion`. Pair it with `relevance=filter` and `relevant_to` to keep only the rows about what you mean. `instagram.include=creator` adds each Instagram creator's declared country, followers and public email, billed by the reel search as on a direct call. For a planned, reranked and clustered answer across more sources, use /v1/search/everywhere.

**Use when** Use it instead of calling several platforms' search endpoints yourself; for a ranked, summarised answer use search/everywhere. **Not for** a ranked, clustered answer with comments attached (search/everywhere), forum threads (search/forums) or news (search/news).
**Cost** price moves with `label` · cache 300 s
**Pricing** Metered, usually 1-14 credits: each platform is billed at its own endpoint's price, per platform, exactly as a direct call to that endpoint is billed (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, Threads, X and Facebook 1 credit a page, Telegram 2, LinkedIn 5). A platform whose page found nothing or failed costs nothing, and a platform page served from cache is free. A Threads phrase that Threads does not recognise is expanded into narrower searches, as on /v1/threads/search, and costs 1 credit per search that returned posts. With expand=context every platform runs your phrase plus expand_queries planned searches (3 by default, 3 at most), each billed as its own page, so the range above is multiplied by 1 plus expand_queries and the estimate quotes it that way. The searches inside a platform judge their rows for free; relevant_to= or label= is billed once on the request, for the rows of the merged page. data.sources.<platform>.credits shows each platform's charge and credits_used the total. Relevance against your query (by default, or with relevance=) is free. Adding relevant_to= holds 8 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 rows that were newly judged: rows already judged for the same topic are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. The default labels (sponsored, intent, niche) are free. label=mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection, or label=intent with offer=, holds 8 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 posts that were newly judged: posts already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** single page - Each platform has its own cursor: continue one platform on its own search endpoint with data.sources.<platform>.next_cursor.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keyword or phrase, sent unchanged to every platform (1-500 characters). Each platform matches it the way its own search endpoint does: Reddit matches any of the words unless you wrap a phrase in double quotes, and a phrase Threads does not recognise is expanded into narrower searches. · e.g. `matcha latte`
- `platforms` (optional, string) - Comma-separated platforms to search: tiktok, instagram, youtube, reddit, threads, twitter, facebook, linkedin, telegram. Default tiktok,instagram,youtube,reddit,threads. Each one costs its own endpoint's page price, and only when its page came back with rows. · e.g. `tiktok,instagram,youtube`
- `since` (optional, string) - Keep only posts published on or after this date on every platform: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. A row with no date is kept. A platform page trimmed to nothing still costs its page, as it would on that platform's own endpoint. When you do not send a platform's own date filter, the narrowest one that reaches this date is sent for you on TikTok, YouTube and Reddit (an exact date on Threads, Facebook and X); data.window says which. · e.g. `2026-09-01`
- `until` (optional, string) - Keep only posts published on or before this date on every platform: YYYY-MM-DD (that whole UTC day is included) or an ISO 8601 timestamp. A row with no date is kept. Sent natively as Threads and Facebook end_date and the X until: operator; the other platforms have no upper bound of their own, so their newer rows are dropped from the page and still cost the page. Use since and until together for a calendar month. · e.g. `2026-09-30`
- `expand` (optional, enum: context) - Optional. context also searches up to three short phrases written from your query and, when you send it, relevant_to: the words the people who wrote the posts actually use. Native search reads a query literally, so a long phrase such as fake byd spare part sellers scam misses a seller who writes BYD spare parts Sharjah. Your own query always runs as well. Every row carries matched_query, the search that found it; data.expansion lists the searches with the rows each one added and its credits; data.sources.<platform>.by_query has each search's own cursor. Each extra search is billed on each platform exactly like your query (1 credit a page with rows, LinkedIn 5), and writing the searches is free. If they cannot be written in time, one search is made from the product words in your query (data._warnings says expand_fallback), or, when there are none to drop, only your query runs (expand_unavailable). Each search on each platform is one in-flight request on your API key, so one expanded call on six platforms holds up to 24 of the key's 50 at once; a search the limit refuses costs nothing and data._warnings says searches_limited.
- `expand_queries` (optional, integer, 1-3) - Optional, only with expand=context. How many extra searches to run, 1 to 3 (default 3). Each one can cost up to one more page per platform.
- `tiktok.date_posted` (optional, enum: yesterday | this-week | this-month | last-3-months | last-6-months | all-time) - TikTok only. Sent to /v1/tiktok/search as `date_posted`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: yesterday, this-week, this-month, last-3-months, last-6-months, all-time.
- `tiktok.sort_by` (optional, enum: relevance | most-liked | date-posted) - TikTok only. Sent to /v1/tiktok/search as `sort_by`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: relevance, most-liked, date-posted.
- `tiktok.region` (optional, string) - TikTok only. Sent to /v1/tiktok/search as `region`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. · e.g. `US`
- `instagram.date_posted` (optional, enum: last-week | last-month | last-year) - Instagram only. Sent to /v1/instagram/search/reels as `date_posted`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: last-week, last-month, last-year.
- `instagram.include` (optional, enum: creator) - Instagram only. Sent to /v1/instagram/search/reels as `include`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: creator.
- `youtube.uploadDate` (optional, enum: today | this_week | this_month | this_year) - YouTube only. Sent to /v1/youtube/search as `uploadDate`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: today, this_week, this_month, this_year.
- `youtube.sortBy` (optional, enum: relevance | popular) - YouTube only. Sent to /v1/youtube/search as `sortBy`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: relevance, popular.
- `youtube.type` (optional, enum: videos | shorts) - YouTube only. Sent to /v1/youtube/search as `type`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: videos, shorts.
- `youtube.duration` (optional, enum: under_3_min | between_3_and_20_min | over_20_min) - YouTube only. Sent to /v1/youtube/search as `duration`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: under_3_min, between_3_and_20_min, over_20_min.
- `youtube.region` (optional, string) - YouTube only. Sent to /v1/youtube/search as `region`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `reddit.sort` (optional, enum: relevance | new | top | comment_count) - Reddit only. Sent to /v1/reddit/search as `sort`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: relevance, new, top, comment_count.
- `reddit.timeframe` (optional, enum: all | day | week | month | year) - Reddit only. Sent to /v1/reddit/search as `timeframe`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: all, day, week, month, year.
- `threads.start_date` (optional, string) - Threads only. Sent to /v1/threads/search as `start_date`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `threads.end_date` (optional, string) - Threads only. Sent to /v1/threads/search as `end_date`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `twitter.sort` (optional, enum: latest | top) - X only. Sent to /v1/twitter/search/tweets as `sort`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: latest, top.
- `facebook.start_date` (optional, string) - Facebook only. Sent to /v1/facebook/search/posts as `start_date`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `facebook.end_date` (optional, string) - Facebook only. Sent to /v1/facebook/search/posts as `end_date`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `facebook.recent_posts` (optional, boolean) - Facebook only. Sent to /v1/facebook/search/posts as `recent_posts`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `facebook.location_uid` (optional, string) - Facebook only. Sent to /v1/facebook/search/posts as `location_uid`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `linkedin.sort_by` (optional, enum: date_posted | relevance) - LinkedIn only. Sent to /v1/linkedin/search/posts as `sort_by`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: date_posted, relevance.
- `linkedin.date_posted` (optional, enum: past_24h | past_week | past_month) - LinkedIn only. Sent to /v1/linkedin/search/posts as `date_posted`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: past_24h, past_week, past_month.
- `linkedin.content_type` (optional, enum: videos | photos | jobs | live_videos | documents | collaborative_articles) - LinkedIn only. Sent to /v1/linkedin/search/posts as `content_type`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: videos, photos, jobs, live_videos, documents, collaborative_articles.
- `telegram.date_posted` (optional, enum: last-hour | last-day | last-week | last-month | last-year) - Telegram only. Sent to /v1/telegram/search as `date_posted`, exactly as that endpoint takes it. One of: last-hour, last-day, last-week, last-month, last-year.
- `telegram.region` (optional, string) - Telegram only. Sent to /v1/telegram/search as `region`, exactly as that endpoint takes it.
- `ai_written_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with label=ai_written and exclude=ai_written. The p (0 to 1) at which exclude=ai_written drops a post. Default 0.95 (level likely). 0.71 also drops possible posts: more AI posts go, and more posts by people with them.
- **Shared controls** `label` (sponsored | mention | intent | niche | quality | ai_style | ai_written | injection; paid: mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection) · `exclude` (engagement_bait | ai_style | ai_written) · `label_evidence` (1) · `brand` · `brand_description` · `offer` · `relevance` (score | filter) · `relevant_to` · `relevance_threshold` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality)

**Constraints**

- `ai_written_threshold` is a no-op without `label` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `relevance_threshold`, `relevant_to` are no-ops without `relevance` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `exclude`, `brand`, `brand_description`, `offer`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 3 comma-separated values.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ platform, post, computed }` (inferred from a sample): {platform string}; `post` {id string, url string, published_at string}; `post.content` {text string, media_urls string, thumbnail_url string, duration_seconds number}; `post.author` {username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, verified boolean}; `post.engagement` {views number, likes number, comments number, shares number, saves number}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned boolean, deleted boolean}; `post.ext` {music_id string, author_id string, author_followers number, download_count number} (+24 more).

Page-level: `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.labels`, `data.relevance`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/search/multi" \
  --data-urlencode "query=matcha latte" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/search/news - 2-62 credits (request-shaped)

Plans your query into search angles, localizes each angle into the language of every requested country edition (one combined LLM call, fail-open), then fans out up to 12 parallel legs per engine and merges the articles into one deduplicated list. Two independent news indexes are available through `engines`: `google` (the default, 50 country editions) and `bing` (49 of those editions). They overlap very little in practice, so asking for both roughly doubles the distinct articles a query returns and is the way to get a text snippet on most rows: the google engine returns headline, publisher, link, image and an exact publish time but rarely a snippet, while the bing engine returns a description on effectively every row. Every article carries `engine` provenance and a `published_at_precision` of `exact` or `approximate`, because the two indexes do not report publish times with the same fidelity. Every leg reports truthful localization provenance: `query_source` says whether its keyword was `translated`, confirmed `original`, or a `fallback_original` after a localization failure. Supports streaming via `Accept: text/event-stream` (the `plan_refined` chunk always carries the expanded legs with per-leg provenance before any leg settles) and sync via `Accept: application/json`. Filters: `publisher` and `from`/`to` exact date windows (google engine only; they pin its legs to the primary source), `time_range` recency, `depth` per-leg article depth, `sort` result ordering, `max_legs` cost cap. Billing is metered and settles down to the work actually done; empty, skipped and failed legs bill 0.

**Use when** you want it for news coverage across several countries at once; for one topic across social platforms use search/everywhere.
**Cost** price moves with `countries`, `engines` · cache 300 s
**Pricing** 2 credits + 1 credit per google leg that returns at least one article (upfront hold 2 + min(5 x countries, max_legs, 12), maximum 14 on the default engine). Adding the bing engine adds 1 credit per 5 articles it returns, because that engine is priced per article rather than per call; the absolute ceiling with both engines is 62. The hold always settles down to the actual charge, and empty, skipped or failed legs bill 0.
**Streaming** Optional SSE - send `Accept: text/event-stream` for incremental frames, or omit it for one JSON body.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - News topic or question (1-500 chars). Boolean AND/OR/NOT and quoted phrases are supported; Google advanced operators (site:, intitle:, before:) are rejected. · e.g. `samsung galaxy launch`
- `countries` (optional, string) - CSV of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to search (1-12 of the 50 supported editions, default US). Each country searches its news edition in its default language; duplicates collapse. · e.g. `KR,US,JP`
- `engines` (optional, string) - CSV of news indexes to search: google (default) and bing. Asking for both runs the same plan on each and merges the results, which roughly doubles distinct articles and adds a snippet to most rows. The bing engine serves 49 of the 50 editions (not CN) and is priced per article; `publisher` and `from`/`to` are google-only. · e.g. `google,bing`
- `sort` (optional, enum: relevance | date) - Ordering of the merged articles: relevance (default, each engine's own ranking) or date (newest first, undated articles last). · e.g. `date`
- `time_range` (optional, enum: day | week | month | year) - Recency window (day | week | month | year, default day). Ignored when from/to is present. · e.g. `week`
- `from` (optional, string) - Lower publish-date bound, YYYY-MM-DD or Unix seconds. Pins every leg to the primary news source. · e.g. `2026-07-01`
- `to` (optional, string) - Upper publish-date bound, YYYY-MM-DD or Unix seconds. Pins every leg to the primary news source. · e.g. `2026-07-31`
- `publisher` (optional, string) - Bare publisher domain filter (e.g. bbc.com; no scheme or path). Pins every leg to the primary news source. · e.g. `bbc.com`
- `depth` (optional, integer, 10-100) - Articles requested per leg (10-100 in steps of 10, default 10). The google engine is priced per call, so depth is free there; the bing engine is priced per article and caps its own legs at 20. · e.g. `10`
- `max_legs` (optional, integer, 1-12) - Hard cap on billable legs (1-12, default 12). The upfront hold shrinks with it. · e.g. `4`
- `group` (optional, enum: stories) - Optional. stories groups the articles that report the same event across editions, outlets and languages into data.stories[] ({ id, head_id, member_ids, size, outlets, outlet_count, countries, languages, first_seen, last_seen, judged }), where every id is an article's canonical_url (or url). items[] and its order are unchanged. data.story_grouping reports how many articles were judged and what it cost. An article that could not be judged is its own story with judged: false; if grouping is unavailable, stories is null and data._warnings says stories_unavailable. JSON responses only (ignored on the event stream). Grouping is on by default now (see judgments); group=stories asks for it explicitly with a longer time budget. Free.
- `judgments` (optional, enum: on | off) - Optional. on (default) or off. On, JSON responses also carry data.stories and data.story_grouping (see group), grouped under a short time budget; when grouping does not finish in time, stories is null and data._warnings says stories_pending (stories_unavailable when it failed). items[], their order and the price are unchanged. off returns the response without them.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {id string, title string, url string, canonical_url string, source_name string, domain string, snippet null, image_url string, published_at string, rank number, placement string, country_code string, language_code string, angle_id string, effective_query string, query_source string, legs_returned string[]}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/search/news" \
  --data-urlencode "query=samsung galaxy launch" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
